@@ -0,0 +1,94 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '80'
+title: Gated fold test loses a late fact when the model writes a large second section
+---
+## What
+
+The gated test `CompactionSmokeIntegrationTests.aPlantedFactLateInTheSpanSurvivesTheFold` fails on the current `main` branch. It is not caused by any change on this branch. It is a real, repeatable failure.
+
+Command: `swift test --package-path IntegrationTests --filter 'CompactionSmokeIntegrationTests'`
+
+Failure text:
+```
+CompactionSmokeIntegrationTests.swift:515:9: Expectation failed: summary.contains(Self.plantedFactValue)
+summary.contains(Self.plantedFactValue) → false
+summary → "1. Intent - The user's request for a summary of the project brief and migration plan, specifically the ingest path replacement and station archive cut-over."
+Self.plantedFactValue → "Kestrel"
+```
+
+I ran this test three times. It failed the same way each time.
+
+## Why it happens
+
+The real model writes a long answer with numbered sections. Section 1 is short.
+Section 2 is long — it holds two long paragraphs, one of which states the
+planted fact "Kestrel" near its end.
+
+`Summarization.cut(_:toCharacters:)` in
+`Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Compaction/Summarization.swift` must shrink
+this answer to fit the span's byte budget. It calls
+`sectionAlignedPrefix(of:withinBytes:)`. That function finds the largest set of
+WHOLE sections that fit the budget. Here, only section 1 fits whole; section 2
+alone is bigger than the room left after section 1.
+
+When the kept sections do NOT run up to the last section header,
+`cut(_:toCharacters:)` returns the section-aligned text right away:
+
+```swift
+let sections = sectionAlignedPrefix(of: summary, withinBytes: limit)
+if let sections, !sections.endsAtFinalSection { return sections.text }
+```
+
+It never compares this against a plain byte-boundary cut, which would keep
+much more of the answer — enough, in this case, to reach "Kestrel". The
+comparison against a byte-boundary cut runs ONLY when the kept sections DO run
+up to the last header (the `^51e9dyq` fix, tested by
+`theFinalSectionIsCutRatherThanDroppedWhole` in
+`Tests/FoundationModelsRouterTests/SummarizationStageTests.swift`).
+
+So this is not a simple bug. It is a real design choice, and it has its own
+test: `theLastResortCutOfASectionedAnswerFallsOnASectionBoundary` in the same
+file asserts that when one more section would not fit, the cut keeps ONLY the
+whole sections already in hand — even if a byte-boundary cut could keep more
+text. The reason given there: a stored summary must never end in the middle of
+a section, because a later turn reads that stored summary as its context, and
+a broken section confuses the model.
+
+So there are two goals in tension:
+1. Never end a stored summary in the middle of a section (existing rule, has
+   its own test).
+2. Keep a fact stated late in the folded span (the rule this new gated test
+   checks).
+
+For this real-model answer, section 2 alone is bigger than the room left after
+section 1, so goal 1 forces the stored summary down to section 1 alone, and
+goal 2 fails.
+
+## What NOT to do
+
+Do not just remove or loosen the `!sections.endsAtFinalSection` short-circuit
+in `cut(_:toCharacters:)`. That would break
+`theLastResortCutOfASectionedAnswerFallsOnASectionBoundary`, which exists for
+a documented reason (`^51e9dyq`): a stored summary that ends mid-section
+becomes bad context for the next turn.
+
+## What to decide
+
+A person needs to pick a resolution, for example:
+- Add a smaller in-between cut: keep the whole sections that fit, THEN add as
+  much of the byte budget as remains from the NEXT section, cut at a sentence
+  or word boundary within that next section (not ending the whole answer
+  mid-section, but also not throwing away all remaining budget room).
+- Or judge that this specific gated test's fixture is unusually large for its
+  budget, and change the fixture so the model's real answer is more likely to
+  fit two whole sections.
+- Or accept this as a known, occasional real-model failure mode and mark it
+  in the test's own history the way `^azd033m`, `^49dy082`, and `^xx02yn6`
+  are marked there already.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `swift test --package-path IntegrationTests --filter 'CompactionSmokeIntegrationTests'` green, three runs in a row.
+- [ ] `swift test` still green (the hermetic `SummarizationStageTests` suite, in particular `theLastResortCutOfASectionedAnswerFallsOnASectionBoundary` and `theFinalSectionIsCutRatherThanDroppedWhole`, must still pass under whatever new rule is chosen). #router #real-model #compaction #test-reproducibility
\ No newline at end of file
